question: How can a health worker tell whether a normal-looking vial of tetanus vaccine was once frozen?
answer: By freezing another vial on purpose. In the shake test, a vial from the same batch is frozen solid, thawed and shaken beside the suspect one. Ice clumps the aluminium particles into heavy flakes that sink fast, leaving clear liquid above. A suspect vial that clears as fast as the control is thrown away.
move: When damage is invisible, make a known-damaged sample to compare against.
source: Kartoglu et al., Bulletin of the WHO, 2010
reference: Kartoglu, Özgüler, Wolfson & Kurzatkowski, Validation of the shake test for detecting freeze damage to adsorbed vaccines, Bulletin of the World Health Organization, 2010
